themes_detail.label: Outdoor Dining Infrastructure Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Outdoor dining complaints exploded to 4 THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average over 8 weeks—a 1500% spike (z-score: 8.66)—suggesting rapid deterioration of sheds, barriers, or sidewalk encroachments in Park Slope's dining corridor that demands immediate investigation into enforcement gaps.
evidence: 4 outdoor dining complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1500% increase, z-score: 8.66)
Statistically highest-severity spike in the dataset, indicating acute new problem rather than chronic issue
No prior community board mentions or budget requests tied to outdoor dining, suggesting this is genuinely new
reporting_angles: Map which streets in Park Slope/Carroll Gardens are seeing the most complaints and visit to document violations
Interview DOT/SLA enforcement about capacity constraints or policy changes that may have triggered enforcement gap

themes_detail.label: Curb Collapse and Sidewalk Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Curb condition complaints jumped to 27 THIS WEEK vs. 6.5 weekly average—a 315% spike (z-score: 5.38)—indicating accelerating street infrastructure decay that overlaps with the district's persistent water main concerns flagged in annual budget requests.
evidence: 27 curb condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 6.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (315% increase, z-score: 5.38)
Convergence: recurring budget request to 'Inspect water main on specific street segment and repair or replace as needed' suggests underlying infrastructure failure
Dead/dying trees also spiked 433% this week (6 vs. 1.1 avg), pointing to possible soil/water system problems affecting multiple infrastructure systems
reporting_angles: Obtain DEP records on water main breaks or repairs in Park Slope/Carroll Gardens this week and map against curb complaints
Interview residents on affected blocks about when damage appeared and whether it correlates with water service issues

themes_detail.label: Commercial Noise Surge
themes_detail.summary: Commercial noise complaints spiked to 26 THIS WEEK vs. 11.2 weekly average—a 131% increase (z-score: 3.01)—suggesting new bar/restaurant openings, construction, or event activity straining residential-commercial boundaries in Park Slope.
evidence: 26 commercial noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 11.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (131% increase, z-score: 3.01)
Overlaps with 1243 DOB building permit filings in last 90 days (757 alterations), suggesting renovation/reopening activity in commercial corridors
4 active ULURP/land use applications (46 Nelson Street rezoning, 444 Carroll Street waterfront certification) may signal commercial intensification
reporting_angles: Cross-reference 311 commercial noise hotspots with recent DOB permits and ULURP applications to identify new venues or construction projects
Interview residents on the most complained-about blocks and community board members about enforcement priorities

themes_detail.label: Homeless Services Request Spike
themes_detail.summary: Homeless person assistance complaints surged to 21 LAST WEEK vs. 4.0 weekly average—a 425% spike (z-score: 3.27)—aligning with the district's recurring budget request for 'Other request for services for the homeless,' indicating growing street-level homelessness or outreach gaps.
evidence: 21 homeless person assistance complaints LAST WEEK vs. 4.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (425% increase, z-score: 3.27)
Convergence: community board has submitted identical budget request year-over-year for 'Other request for services for the homeless,' indicating chronically unmet need
Obstruction complaints also spiked 167% this week (9 vs. 3.4 avg), potentially linked to homeless encampments blocking sidewalks
reporting_angles: Interview DHS about capacity and outreach resources allocated to Park Slope/Carroll Gardens; obtain street count data for the district
Visit shelters and outreach sites serving this area to understand whether surge reflects new need, seasonal pattern, or resource constraint
Profile residents experiencing homelessness on key corridors (Prospect Park West, etc.) to document quality-of-life impact

themes_detail.label: Dead Tree Infestation or Disease Event
themes_detail.summary: Dead/dying tree complaints jumped to 6 THIS WEEK vs. 1.1 weekly average—a 433% spike (z-score: 4.63)—suggesting possible pest infestation, disease outbreak, or water stress affecting the district's tree canopy, relevant to the recurring park upgrade budget requests.
evidence: 6 dead/dying tree complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (433% increase, z-score: 4.63)
Convergence: community board requests 'Reconstruct or upgrade a park or amenity' and 'Damaged Tree' remains top-10 complaint (333 total over 90 days)
Curb condition spike this week may indicate common root cause (water main failure, soil compaction) affecting both trees and pavement

Photograph and document affected trees; interview residents about timing and visible symptoms
